title: Developer SprintStarter: integration snapshot asset pack for API/SDK onboarding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Deliver a compact, modular asset pack for API/SDK onboarding docs aimed at first-time integrators. The pack includes: 1) a 6-card 'SprintStarter' microflow set (light + dark variants) that visually summarizes Authenticate -> Install -> First Call -> Stream -> Tool Call -> Troubleshoot; 2) three production-ready full-width screenshots of Console auth setup and SDK snippet execution; 3) 8-frame PNG sprite for streaming progress animation with a matching reduced-motion SVG; 4) small key-rotation micro-illustrations and a 'safe fallback' state for expired-keys; 5) template screenshots for both macOS and Windows terminal sizes and a mobile breakpoint for docs; 6) handoff-ready export (SVG, 2x PNG, WebP) and a short README for engineers describing naming conventions and suggested CDN paths.
acceptance_criteria: Figma master file updated with final frames and a published component library link
All assets exported in required formats and named using the docs-assets naming scheme: docs-assets/{release}/developer-sprintstarter/{asset-name}-{variant}.{ext}
Light and dark variants across all cards; color contrast passes WCAG AA for all text layers
Streaming sprite has an accessible reduced-motion SVG alternative and a 8-frame PNG sprite with consistent 64px height
Console screenshots match production UI (no placeholder text) and reference real config values redacted via placeholder tokens
Handoff PR in github.com/redwood-inference/docs has the assets added and a short usage table in the README
Design sign-off from PM (Ethan Cho) and engineering review ack from ENG owners (ENG-4120)
A short style note (max 250 words) is present explaining when to use cards vs full screenshots in the docs

design_notes: Trade-off: Keep the SprintStarter set to 6 cards to cover core flows while limiting translator/localization overhead.
Prefer SVG icons for scalability; export PNG/WebP for older browsers as part of the README guidance.
Stream animation should be a neutral, low-motion sequence; provide reduced-motion path to respect user settings.
Screenshots must use placeholder tokens and the official redwood terminal theme. Produce both macOS and Windows variants for documentation fidelity.
Avoid showing internal metrics in screenshots; use synthetic but realistic-looking latency/cost numbers to keep examples believable.
If timeline slips, drop the optional 'tokenless dev sandbox' variant; ensure core deliverables ship on schedule.
